chapter_theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 5 of 21): the rotting body, the funeral and Death's men, women's eyes and the poet's wasted verse, false promisers, and the miser who gives not even bran, set against pleas for the abode of supreme wisdom, the word of grace already received, and the feet; the praise leans on the Mahabharata and Krishna as Murugan's uncle.
structure_note: Three refrain groups: 1052 and 1053 close the கருணை மேருவே run; 1054 to 1058 end in சிகரி தகர வீக்கிய or முதிய மூர்த்திகள் தம்பிரானே; 1059 to 1063 share the refrain குலிச பார்த்திபன் உலகு காத்தருள் கோவே தேவே வேளே வானோர் பெருமாளே, with Kurukshetra and Gajendra in the praise; 1064 to 1066 are short songs ending அறிவும் உரமும் அறமும் நிறமும் அழகும் உடைய பெருமாளே.

1052.reading: After playing with women of sandal-smeared breasts and Kama's arrows, the poet heaps names on himself: one who fawns shamelessly, dallies, is worthless, a dog, sinful, cruel, a babbler without learning, blind and seeking nothing, and asks whether there will be a day when Murugan rules him. The praise says that, sent by the father whom Vishnu could not find, Murugan as Madurai's lord mounted the seat of learning and examined all four, and calls him Meru of compassion, rider of the peacock.
1052.nuance: The run of self-names (குனகுவேனை, குறையனேனை, நாயேனை, வினையேனை, கொடியனேனை, குதலையேனை, குருடனேனை) makes the confession. மதுரேசன் அரிய சாரதா பீடம் அதனில் ஏறி அகில நாலும் ஆராயும் may allude to Murugan judging the poems of the Madurai academy, but which story and what 'all four' means is not clear from the text.

1053.reading: The poet asks Murugan to come dancing on his peacock while all dance: the serpent Adisesha below, Meru, Kali and Siva on his bull who danced against her, ghosts and vetalas, Sarasvati and Brahma, the gods, the moon, and Lakshmi and tall Vishnu as Murugan's in-laws. The praise recalls Bhima with his mace and Arjuna's arrows reducing the enemy armies, the bellowing cattle brought back, and Vishnu who reclines on the ocean and rides Garuda, Murugan's uncle, and names him Lord who dwells in the heart of the great king Prabhuda Deva.
1053.nuance: The whole plea is a cosmic dance with every figure joining (ஆட repeated), ending மயிலும் ஆடி நீ ஆடி வரவேணும். வனச மாமியார், நெடிய மாமனார: Lakshmi and Vishnu as mother- and father-in-law, since Murugan's wives are counted Vishnu's daughters. ப்ரபுட தேவ மாராஜன் names a king, the only patron named in this chapter. கேர்டுதி is corrupt.

1054.reading: The poet confesses cherishing without sense the body, a hut covered with skin over blood, brain, flesh, excrement and phlegm, a bubble on pit water that bursts, food for vultures, dogs, ghouls and crows, sinking in the world in vain, and asks Murugan to tell him the abode of supreme wisdom that ritualists who strew flowers and shoots in showy rites cannot see. The praise names him child of Uma, wife of the ash-smeared Siva, delighting as sages and gods praise him in song, whose vel powdered serpent, Meru and seas while ghouls and Kali danced on the battlefield.
1054.nuance: குழிநீர் மேல் குமிழி போல: the body as a bubble on standing water. The ritualists are dismissed as நாடக ஆசார கிரியையாளர், rites like a stage play. The closing question repeats 1049's formula word for word.

1055.reading: The poet, staggering day and night to quench the hunger-fire burning in his sagging body, asks: when the quarrels of logicians of every creed are ended and one worships the lotus feet with the tongue, and becomes a form of knowledge beyond turiya and beyond all instruments, thrilled, the breath stilled, will Kama's flower arrows strike those pure ones? The praise recalls the Kurukshetra war in which the hundred fell by Arjuna, and Krishna who went once as envoy, Murugan's uncle, and the vel that made the ocean cry out and shattered the hill.
1055.nuance: சகல சமய தார்க்கிகர் கலகம் ஒழிய: the quarrel of the creeds' debaters must end before worship. The question is rhetorical: Kama's arrows (ரதிபதி விடு பூக்கணை) cannot touch one who has passed beyond the instruments, so the plea is for that state. ஒரு தூது திரியும் அரி is Krishna's embassy to the Kauravas.

1056.reading: Before Yama binds him, while daughter, wife, mother's kin and all who come wail and cry out inside and outside the house and Death's men with fire-spitting eyes shout, the poet asks to praise Murugan's anklets with his tongue, calling him the Murugan who showed his claim on those who dwell as the ages and their end, the moon's course, being and non-being. The praise recalls Arjuna whose bow destroyed the horses, elephants and chariots of Dhritarashtra's sons and Krishna who relieved the earth's burden, and the vel that pierced Sura when he took the form of mountain and sea.
1056.nuance: The deathbed is crowded with named kin (மகள், மனைவி, தாய்க்குலம்) whose wailing is useless against Yama's men. The second clause of the plea is hard to split; its sense of Murugan as one whom even beings beyond time melt toward is a guess. ஡ stands for ஊ in உடலூடே.

1057.reading: The body is a hut of guts, water, fat and excrement on many bones, set up as a home for cruel disease, with life said to be in it; before Death's men come to fight for it, the poet asks whether Murugan will not give him the flawless truth so that his mind may ripen and praise his feet. The praise names Kanda who, becoming a vengai tree in the forest of the hunters, loved and secretly united with the Kuratti, and the Lord of the ancient gods who gazed at his endless form.
1057.nuance: மதியும் மூத்து: the mind ripening, as if wisdom were a matter of maturing, not escape. The vengai tree and களவு belong to the Valli story. வடிவிலாப் புலமதனை நாட்டிடு is obscure.

1058.reading: The poet marvels at the word of grace Murugan spoke that killed his five senses and instruments and turned death away from him: a word common to all and the one first source, the meaning of the Vedas beyond day and night, the end of all meaning, great open space, the endless goal, inconceivable, nectar to drink. The praise names the vel that made the ocean cry out, the mighty peacock, the son of Parvati who drank at the breasts of the Krittika women, and the Lord of the ancient gods of lotus, milk sea and mountain.
1058.nuance: Unusually the plea is in the past tense: கருணை வார்த்தை இருந்தவாறு என், 'how was that word of grace!', marvelling at a teaching already received. மரணம் மாற்றிய: the word has turned death away. பெருவெளியதாய் names the teaching as vast space.

1059.reading: The poet confesses that he does not sing or seek the vel that withered the great mango tree rising from the salt sea, to reach liberation, does not fall at the ringing feet full of compassion, nor even at the feet of those who fall at them, does not give without delay even a handful of bran to those who ask, and so dies without having lived; he asks Murugan to grant him worth and liberation forever. The praise tells how the elephant gripped by the crocodile cried 'Narayana, Gopala, save!' and Vishnu came on Garuda and crushed its head, and calls Murugan his nephew and protector of Indra's world.
1059.nuance: The confession is a list of omissions, each worse than the last: not singing, not falling at the feet, not falling even at the devotees' feet (வீழ்வார் கால் மீதினும் வீழேன்), not giving even bran (தவிடின் ஆர்ப் பதம்). வாழாதே சாவது: to die without having lived.

1060.reading: The poet asks whether he must go round without being saved, not wearing or seeking the feet that darkness cannot enter of the boundless reality that is sun, moon, earth, sky, water, fire, wind, the stars, the days of the week, the twenty-seven asterisms, the seven worlds, the Veda and the light beyond it, Brahma, Vishnu and, above them, Sivam. The praise recalls the eighteen days in which the hundred sons of Dhritarashtra fell while Partha was protected by Krishna, Murugan's uncle, and names Murugan of the vel and kadamba on his peacock.
1060.nuance: The list climbs from the elements and time (கிழமை, பதினாலு ஆறு ஏழாம் நாள், the 27 stars) through the gods to மேலே சிவமான தொலைவிலாப் பொருள். இருள் புகாக் கழல்: feet no darkness enters. The line naming Krishna is corrupt (஧த்ருர் கோமான்).

1061.reading: As youth passes and the body goes, drums sound, the house rings with 'ko ko', the child cries, the wife cries, the mother falls crying 'my life', and the funeral journey enters Death's town, the poet asks Murugan to come on that day and say to Death 'go' and to him 'return'. The praise names the hero who routed the asuras amid the hunters' cries in the millet field, the babbling child-guru who taught even his father, the six-syllabled one, with form and without.
1061.nuance: தாதையும் ஓதும் குதலை வாய்க் குருபர: the child who with a babbling mouth taught even his father, the teaching of Siva. சடாக்ஷர is the six-syllable mantra of Murugan. The plea's last words (வாரா வானாள் போநாம் நீ மீள்) are hard to split, and பா஡ண is corrupt, perhaps பூரண.

1062.reading: The poet, who sang verses on women who say 'come to the house', asking whether their eyes are sword, vel, carp or deer, their dark curling hair cloud, forest or Mayon's form, their coral mouths milk, honey, syrup or the gods' nectar, asks whether he, a dog, must perish without being saved. The praise shows Murugan running as Parvati watches melting, crying to Sura 'don't go, turn back' as the asuras wail and the ocean burns, the vel that pierced the Krauncha hill, and calls him treasure of the one under the banyan.
1062.nuance: The confession is about the poet's own craft: the string of 'is it this or that?' comparisons is the love poetry he wasted on courtesans (கவி பாடா நாயேன்), as in 1039 he wasted praise on patrons. ஆல் கீழ் வாழ்வார் is Siva seated under the banyan.

1063.reading: The poet says women's eyes like Death's vels have killed the way, path and dharma of Vedic recitation, his courage, shining knowledge and fortune have left, and he has become a mound water cannot climb, where weeds spring up in what falls; he asks the hero to look and rule him so that he does not go in vain. The praise calls Murugan son of the one who felled Death, whom Vishnu could not see, treasure of those who daily recite his flawless feet with full mouths, and the vel that drove the asura chiefs into the sea.
1063.nuance: நீர் ஏறாதோர் மேடாய்: a raised patch the water never reaches, where only weeds grow, the poet's barren life. மறலி சாய்த்தவர், the one who felled Death, is Siva. Several splits in the plea are uncertain.

1064.reading: Before quarrelsome Death destroys all the lust that, through women's cruel eyes in lovemaking, drew him with delight into this rotting hut that runs with blood, the poet asks Murugan to come in compassion on the golden peacock, its beauty pouring. The praise names the vel that split the hill the sun circles, the hero who chased the asura chief across the conch-filled sea, the son of the Lord who burned Rati's husband, and the lotus face too beautiful to draw.
1064.nuance: இரதி பதியை எரி செய்தருளும் இறைவர் குமர: Murugan as son of the Lord who burned Kama, set against the lust of the plea. எழுத அரிய, the beauty that cannot be drawn.

1065.reading: The poet asks when there will be a day free of the trickery of those who say 'your sorrow will end and your poverty go; you will easily get the nectar drink, the wish-cow and the magic pill; to end our wasting hunger give us curd and rice, anklets, bracelets and necklaces and gold plates to melt'. The praise names the vel that pierced the high hill and the asuras' chests and split the ocean's belly, the hero on the peacock who broke the gods' fetters, possessed of knowledge, strength, virtue, splendour and beauty.
1065.nuance: The speakers are not named. They promise wonders (அமிர்த சுரபானம், சுரபி, குளிகை, the alchemical pill) and ask for food and gold, which suggests false wonder-workers rather than courtesans. இவ்விரகு தவிர்வது ஒருநாளே asks for release from this deceit.

1066.reading: Since ornaments, wealth, jewelled clothes, old servants and wife will not come with him on the hard journey when life leaves, and kin of good heart will gather only to lay the body on firewood, the poet asks Murugan, before that cruelty, to grant that he, his servant, speak of his feet so that they are pleased. The praise calls him the matchless one of Arunai and Palani, the old one and the young lord, who embraced the hunters' peacock-like girl after worshipping her with both hands.
1066.nuance: பகரில் ஒருவர் வருக அரிய பயணம்: no one comes on that journey. கிழவ இளைய pairs 'old' and 'young' as epithets. இருகை தொழுது புணர்: Murugan worships Valli with folded hands before union. அடிமை அடிகள் குளிர மொழிவது may also mean that the feet speak coolly to the servant.

links.note: Both close with the same question, பரம ஞான வீடு ஏது புகல்வாயே. 1049 defines that abode by what cannot touch it; 1054 sets it against the rotting body and against rituals performed for show.

Both see the body as a bubble that forms and bursts (the Naladiyar's மொக்குள், 1054's குமிழி); the Naladiyar praises those who see it so and resolve to end birth, and 1054 confesses cherishing it anyway.
Both say nothing goes with a person at death; the Naladiyar names deeds as the one thing that does, while 1066 lists wealth, servants and wife that do not and turns to praising the feet.

The song builds a cosmic dance verb by verb: Adisesha, Meru, Kali, Siva, ghosts, Sarasvati, Brahma, the gods and the moon all dance (ஆட), and then Murugan with his peacock (மயிலும் ஆடி நீ ஆடி வரவேணும்). Tirumanthiram 2789 builds the same chain, tattvas, Sadasiva, mind, Shakti and the world dancing (ஆட) until the Father dances the dance of bliss. Both use the repeated ஆட to make the god's dance the last step of a world already dancing.

The song makes the end of the quarrels of all creeds' debaters (சகல சமய தார்க்கிகர் கலகம் ஒழிய) the first step toward worship of the feet and a knowledge beyond turiya. Tirumanthiram 1533 says those who saw the six sects did not see him and he is not what they hold (ஆறு சமயப் பொருளும் அவனலன்), then calls for clarity. Both set the arguments of the creeds aside before the Lord can be reached.

The song pictures daughter, wife and mother's kin wailing inside and outside the house (புறமும் ஆர்த்திட) as Yama's men close in, and asks for grace to praise the anklets before then. Tirumanthiram 157 follows the same wailing kin, wives and children (ஆர்த்தெழு சுற்றமும் பெண்டிரும் மக்களும்) only to the edge of the town, where they turn back and burn him. Both show the kin's outcry as unable to go further, which is why the song turns to the feet.

Naladiyar 35 says those who took the body's fruit early, as one takes jaggery from the cane, feel no distress when Death comes (கூற்றம் வருங்கால் பரிவதிலர்). The song asks for the flawless truth so that the mind may ripen and praise the feet (மதியும் மூத்து உனது அடிகள் ஏத்திட) before Death's men come to fight for the hut of bones and disease. Both make the use of the body before Death the answer to Death.

The song marvels at the word of grace that killed the five senses and the instruments and turned death away (புலன் ஐந்தும் மாயக் கரணம் மாய்த்து எனை மரணம் மாற்றிய கருணை வார்த்தை). Tirumanthiram 134 says those who feel beyond words what the teacher speaks (ஆரியன் செப்பும் உரையற்று உணர்வோர்) mix with the shoreless light when the body falls. Both make the guru's spoken word the means of passing beyond the senses and death.

The song lists the poet's failures: he does not fall at the feet, nor even at the feet of those who fall at them (வீழ்வார் கால் மீதினும் வீழேன்), and does not give even bran to those who ask. Tirumanthiram 1857 joins those two failures: what is given to the walking temple, the devotee (நடமாடக் கோயில்), reaches the god in the temple of images. The Tirumanthiram shows why neglect of devotees and of giving is neglect of the Lord.

Naladiyar 91 says those who give gladly what they can even when they have little (இல்லா விடத்தும் இயைந்த அளவினால்) will not find the door of that world shut. The song confesses not giving even a handful of bran (தவிடின் ஆர்ப் பதம் எனினும்) to those who ask, and calls this dying without having lived. The measure is the same in both: giving is judged by what one could give, however little.

The song lists the Lord as sun, moon, earth, sky, water, fire, wind, the stars and the days, the Vedas and the light beyond them, and above them Sivam (மேலே சிவமான தொலைவிலாப் பொருள்). Tirumanthiram 2671 says the yogic god is earth, water, fire, air and sky (மண்ணு நீரனல் காலொடு வானுமாய்) and that his form is beyond even the sky. Both name the Lord as the elements and then place him beyond them.

The song asks Murugan to come on the day of the funeral journey into Death's town and say to Death 'go' and to the poet 'return'. Tirumanthiram 2050 says the true guru set his feet on his devotees' heads and kept away the band of Yama's messengers (தவிரவைத்தான் நமன் தூதுவர் கூட்டம்). The Tirumanthiram states as done what the song asks for.

The song opens the funeral with drums sounding (படு பறைகள் ஆர்த்தெழ) and the household crying. Naladiyar 24 counts the drum beats, once, again, and at the third the corpse is covered and the fire lifted (முக்காலைக் கொட்டினுள்), the dying carrying the dead. The Naladiyar takes the drums as proof that no one escapes; the song uses the same scene to ask Murugan to turn Death back.

The song confesses the love poetry the poet made for courtesans: are their eyes sword or vel, their hair cloud or forest, their mouths milk or nectar (பாலோ தேனோ பாகோ வானோர் அமுதேயோ). Naladiyar 41 mocks the 'worthies' who cry 'O fair, lovely girl' (மாக்கேழ் மடநல்லாய் என்றரற்றும் சான்றவர்) without seeing that the body is a flimsy dwelling. The Naladiyar names the blindness the song confesses in its own praise-verses.

The song calls the poet's life a mound the water never climbs (நீர் ஏறாதோர் மேடாய்) where weeds spring up from what falls in deeds (வினையூடே விழுவினால் களை எழும்). Tirumanthiram 1695 also pictures deeds as weeds (விழலார் விறலாம் வினை) and says they go when the Lord takes his seat in a purified mind. The song gives the barren field; the Tirumanthiram gives the clearing it asks for.

The song says lust, through women's eyes, drew the poet with delight into the rotting hut that runs with blood (குருதி ஒழுகி அழுகும் அவல குடிலை இனிது புகலாலே). Naladiyar 48 asks whether those who praise sandal paste and garlands have not seen vultures tear at the stinking cart (முடைச்சாகாடு) once its axle breaks. Both set desire's delight against the body that rots.

The song quotes people who promise the nectar drink, the wish-cow and the magic pill (அமிர்த சுரபானம் சுரபி குளிகை) and in return ask for curd, rice and gold, and asks for a day free of that trickery (விரகு). Tirumanthiram 2045 calls false gurus those who have looked over mantra, yoga and release but turn blind for the sake of food (ஊண்பொருட்டு அந்தகர் ஆவோர்). The song gives the practice in the street that the Tirumanthiram names in principle.

source_issues: 1059: கனகேர்டு in line 14 is corrupt, perhaps for a word naming Garuda.
1061: பா஡ண in line 14 is corrupt, perhaps பூரண.
